Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — Skill Dreaming, a PR-driven evolving repository skill library for coding agents, evaluated on SWE-bench Pro/Verified and six repositories against a no-skill base agent, five skill-learning baselines and ablations

Skill Dreaming (no version). Baselines: base mini-swe-agent without skills, append-only skills, Trace2Skill, Learning to Commit, SkillLens, CODESKILL, Socratic-SWE; BM25/dense/hybrid retrieval listed as baselines (no results reported); Single Sample and Best-of-N in Table 8

Repository-specific skill library: skills written by a fixed-weight LLM writer from predefined templates (when it applies, how to implement, how to validate), in five families (PR Detection, PR Construction, Feature Implementation, Maintenance Completion, Skill Evolution); each skill keeps supporting PR records, repository-version info, dependencies, related skills; PR-record index with labels usable/repairable/outdated/irrelevant/unsafe. No requirements specification

Per request (Algorithm 1): (1) PR record construction: feature localization, retrieve/segment historical PRs, classify, construct candidates by reuse/repair/synthesis, verify with tests; (2) skill generation and alignment (Add, Update, Specialize, Extend, Conflict, Supersede, Keep); (3) skill-guided implementation: retrieve bounded skills, inject into actor, implement code + tests/docs/config, verify, bounded repair; record outcomes for next round
